job_92b1827d6efec197: USNH Employees should apply within Workday through the Jobs Hub app The Center for Coastal and Ocean Mapping at the University of New Hampshire (UNH) seeks a Postdoctoral Research Associate for a seabed sensing research project focused on characterizing the upper-layer geoacoustic properties of deep-water seaﬂoors. The position will support research involving acoustic sensing technologies, data analysis, model development, and signal processing techniques for seabed characterization. The position is budgeted for an initial two-year period and may transition to a full-time Research Scientist or Research Faculty role upon successful completion. The Postdoctoral Research Associate will be jointly advised by Drs. Larry Mayer, Anthony Lyons, Thomas Blanford, and John Hughes-Clarke and will function as part of a small interdisciplinary team of researchers from academia, industry, and government. The position is based at the Center for Coastal and Ocean Mapping facility on the Durham, NH campus and may include opportunities to participate in at-sea experiments for further data collection and testing. Duties/Responsibilities Research & Analysis (90%) Develop new techniques to characterize the upper-layer geoacoustic properties of deep-water seafloors. Analyze field data collected from split-aperture echosounders, multibeam echosounders, synthetic aperture sonar systems, and scaled laboratory experiments. Develop and validate models for the acoustic scattering properties of mixed-composition seafloors. Use acoustic scattering models to identify signal processing strategies for seabed characterization. Develop algorithms to identify specific seabed characteristics. Conduct independent research related to underwater active acoustics and seabed sensing. Collaborate with researchers from academia, industry, and government as part of an interdisciplinary research team. Participate in field data collection and testing activities, which may include at-sea experiments. Present research findings at professional meetings and scientific conferences. Collaboration and Reporting (10%) Assist with the preparation of progress reports, conference papers, and journal articles. Work closely with project investigators in the execution of sponsored research activities. Assist in mentoring students and staff working on related research activities. Requirements Minimum Acceptable Education & Experience: Ph.D. in Acoustics, Electrical Engineering, Oceanography, Ocean Engineering, Geophysics, or a related field. Familiarity with underwater active acoustics. Experience with common acoustical signal processing techniques, including cross-spectra, auto-spectra, matched filtering, and related methods. Demonstrated ability to work independently and as part of a group. Knowledge, Skills & Abilities: Knowledge of underwater active acoustics and acoustic sensing systems. Knowledge of acoustical signal processing techniques. Ability to analyze and interpret acoustic datasets. Strong analytical, research, and problem-solving skills. Effective written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a research environment. Other Requirements: Ability to participate in field activities and at-sea experiments as required. Preferred Qualiﬁcations : Experience with split-aperture echosounders, multibeam echosounders, and/or synthetic aperture sonar systems. Experience developing acoustic scattering models. Experience applying acoustical signal processing techniques to seafloor characterization problems. Experience working as part of an interdisciplinary research team. Experience conducting field- and laboratory-based research. job_a46b4d86542d2f7f: Overview The mission of the Jean Mayer USDA Human Nutrition Research Center on Aging at Tufts University (HNRCA) is to promote healthy aging through nutrition science to empower people seeking to enjoy long, active, and independent lives. HNRCA investigators conduct the world's most advanced studies on nutrition and aging. The research focuses on determining the nutrient and physical activity requirements necessary to promote well-being for older adults. HNRCA scientists examine how nutrition and physical activity play a major role in the prevention of the major chronic degenerative conditions and diseases associated with aging. What You'll Do The HNRCA invites applications for a Postdoctoral Scholar position within the Biology of Aging research group, under the mentorship of Dr. Arpit Sharma. This role focuses on identifying organelle pathways that regulate longevity and healthy aging. Current projects include: Role of Peroxisomes in Healthy Aging: Conducting C. elegans based lifespan assays, multi-omics analysis, pharmacological and dietary interventions, and high-resolution microscopy to access the role of peroxisome and organelle function in longevity and healthy aging. Role of Lipid Metabolism in Aging: Using cell culture and C. elegans based assays to identify how dietary lipids regulate healthy aging and organelle function. The lab aims to use C. elegans as a model to study the effect of dietary lipids on longevity, while using cell-based methods to dissect molecular mechanisms underpinning the regulation. Novel Projects: The HNRCA offers a unique environment where several molecular aspects of healthy aging are being studied. The position is suitable for working with collaborators and developing new hypotheses and collaborative mechanistic directions in healthy aging. Mitigation Efforts: Research on reducing greenhouse gas emissions, transitioning to renewable energy sources, and promoting energy efficiency in sectors such as transportation, industry, and agriculture. Climate-Related Public Health: Exploring the intersection of climate change and health, focusing on topics like air quality, heat stress, waterborne diseases, and the broader impacts on mental and physical well-being. Water Resource Management: Addressing water scarcity, glacier retreat, and sustainable management of transboundary water systems, which are of critical importance in the South Asian context. Biodiversity and Ecosystem Protection: Projects that aim to preserve biodiversity, protect natural habitats, and explore nature-based solutions for mitigating the impacts of climate change. Climate Policy and Governance: Analyses of regional and national policies, governance mechanisms, and frameworks to enhance climate action, including the role of public-private partnerships and international cooperation. Technology and Innovation: Exploring new technologies, data analytics, and innovative approaches that can accelerate climate action, with an emphasis on scalable solutions suitable for the South Asian context.
